newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union boss - no patent cure for joblessness.
newsitem.headline: German union boss - no patent cure for joblessness.

text.p: Ursula Engelen-Kefer, deputy chief of the German trade union federation DGB, warned on Wednesday that people should not expect too much from the two-day union organised jobs conference in Berlin.
"We should not push expectations too high. There are no patent cures on offer," Engelen-Kefer told German radio.

Responding to criticism that the jobs conference was nothing more than a talking shop, Engelen-Kefer said there had been some progress in Tuesday's discussions between union leaders, politicians and business representatives.
She said in particular there had been progress in the discussion of how to reduce non-wage labour costs, for example by refinancing current social security contributions through other taxes.
She added there had also been signs of agreement on the need for investment in new product areas and innovations.

On Tuesday, Germany's labour office announced that unadjusted unemployment - the most politically sensitive jobs figure in Germany - fell to 4.48 million from February's post-war record of 4.67 million.
